notes: Moses father in law is read as rule 29's possessive recasting, the rectum standing before its head noun, with the compound father in law fusing under rule 30.
Both benefactive lamed phrases are `unrepresented` under rule 40, their suffixes taking the bare English objects.
The he of לְכָה is tagged Sh, so it is `unrepresented` under rule 32's first sentence rather than treated as a directive he.
do thee good is a light verb plus complement headed on good (rule 44), discontinuous around the object pronoun.
